item.text:
{"source":"import Base

# B3/S23 asks for three in either view: the ring, or the ring plus its center.
def Life.three(cell: U32, +ring: U32) -> U32:
  Bool.to_u32(
    Bool.or(
      U32.is_eq(ring, 3),
      U32.is_eq((ring + cell : U32), 3)))

# Cut the flat board into rows and cap every row with dead cells.
def Life.halo(
  height: Nat,
  +width: Nat,
  +cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, List<&2, U32>>:
  match height:
    case 0n:
      Nil{}
    case 1n+rest:
      (0 <> List.append(
        &2,
        U32,
        List.take(&2, U32, cells, width),
        [0])) <>
        Life.halo(
          rest,
          width,
          List.drop(&2, U32, cells, width))

# Three columns advance together across three haloed rows.
def Life.focus(
  +north: List<&2, U32>,
  +middle: List<&2, U32>,
  +south: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match north middle south:
    case nw <> north1 w <> middle1 sw <> south1:
      match north1 middle1 south1:
        case n <> north2 cell <> middle2 s <> south2:
          match north2 middle2 south2:
            case ne <> nt e <> mt se <> st:
              +ring = (
                nw + n + ne
                + w + e
                + sw + s + se : U32)
              Life.three(cell, ring) <>
                Life.focus(north1, middle1, south1)
            case _ _ _:
              Nil{}
        case _ _ _:
          Nil{}
    case _ _ _:
      Nil{}

# The same three-wide focus advances one row at a time down the haloed board.
def Life.sweep(
  +rows: List<&2, List<&2, U32>>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match rows:
    case Nil{}:
      Nil{}
    case north <> tail:
      match tail:
        case Nil{}:
          Nil{}
        case middle <> after:
          match after:
            case Nil{}:
              Nil{}
            case south <> rest:
              List.append(
                &2,
                U32,
                Life.focus(north, middle, south),
                Life.sweep(tail))

def step(
  width: U32,
  height: U32,
  cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  +w = U32.to_nat(width)
  h = U32.to_nat(height)
  +dead = List.replicate(U32, Nat.add(w, 2n), 0)
  Life.sweep(
    dead <>
      List.append(
        &2,
        List<&2, U32>,
        Life.halo(h, w, cells),
        [dead]))

def evolve(
  turns: Nat,
  +width: U32,
  +height: U32,
  cells: List<&2, U32>
) -> List<&2, U32>:
  match turns:
    case 0n:
      cells
    case 1n+rest:
      evolve(rest, width, height, step(width, height, cells))
","hypothesis":"Represent the board as a dead-haloed nested tape. Horizontal triples move across three rows while the same three-wide focus moves vertically across the row tape. The rule itself collapses B3/S23 to one idea: exactly three either around the cell or including its center. This should improve conceptual compression, anticipation, and payoff while preserving the already observed semantics.","findings":"Confirmed: the prior implementation passed all reported behavior and semantic checks. Confirmed style weakness: `peek`, accumulator-driven row splitting, and separate boundary defaults obscured the shared sliding-window structure. This revision removes those mechanisms, constructs one explicit dead halo, uses parallel three-column and three-row sweeps, and replaces the branching survival formula with the equivalent `ring == 3 or ring + cell == 3` relation. No semantic finding was reported."}
